candidates.source_name: e-Prokurimi / Elektronske javne nabavke Kosova (KRPP/ZRJN e-procurement platform, Serbian-language interface & legislation)
candidates.why_relevant: Kosovo's central e-procurement platform is the legally mandated publication point for tender notices, contract award notices and tender dossiers of ALL contracting authorities, including the Serb-majority municipalities (Severna Mitrovica, Zvecan, Zubin Potok, Leposavic, Gracanica, Strpce, Klokot, Ranilug, Partes, Novo Brdo). Kosovo's procurement law requires notices in Albanian, Serbian and English, so this is the single richest Serbian-language source for banking/payment-services awards. Confirmed Serbian-language secondary legislation is hosted at /HOME/Documents/Legislation/.../srb/.
candidates.access_status: public, no login for notice browsing; bidder account needed for dossiers
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of notice-search result pages filtered by CPV/contract type and by contracting authority = the 10 Serb-majority municipalities; download Serbian-language notice PDFs; parse 'OBAVESTENJE O DODELI UGOVORA' forms
candidates.discovered_via_method: sr-language web search on portal name + OSHP
queries_used: e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net elektronske javne nabavke Kosovo srpski OSHP organ za razmatranje nabavki

negative_findings.description: No specific Serbian-language tender or award notice for BANKING or PAYMENT services by a Serb-majority Kosovo municipality (Severna Mitrovica, Zvecan, Zubin Potok, Leposavic, Gracanica, Strpce, Klokot, Ranilug, Partes, Novo Brdo) was surfaced by general web search, despite multiple sr-language query formulations.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search engines surfaced the portals and the notice-form templates but not individual banking/payment award records; such notices appear to live inside portal search interfaces and PDF attachments that general indexes do not reach.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be covered by web search alone - collection must go through portal-internal search (e-prokurimi, prokurimihapur) rather than crawling the open web.

negative_findings.description: Several candidate URLs were identified only from search-result metadata and were not fetched in this pass (kosovo-online.com canonical domain, ekosova.rks-gov.net, Gracanica Online's own domain, EPS Elektrokosmet's dedicated procurement page).
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs are provided with reduced confidence_score; no liveness claim is made.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve these before they enter the monitoring list; a 403/timeout on any of them should be treated as bot-defence, not death.

negative_findings.description: No established Serbian-language term set was found in this pass for modern payment-acceptance concepts as used in Kosovo procurement (e.g. POS terminals, card acquiring, instant payments). Serbian sources use Serbia-standard terms (POS terminali, prihvatanje kartica, instant placanja) whose actual usage in Kosovo Serbian-language tender text is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Glossary built confidently for procurement mechanics (ugovorni organ, obavestenje o dodeli ugovora, ekonomski operater, tenderska dokumentacija) but not for payment-technology nouns.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword filters built on Serbia-standard payments vocabulary may miss or over-match Kosovo Serbian-language notices, which are often translations from Albanian and use calqued wording.

negative_findings.description: It was not established whether the Serb-majority municipalities that operate parallel Serbia-recognised administrations publish procurement anywhere other than the Kosovo portal and their rks-gov.net sites - i.e. whether a parallel municipal procurement publication channel exists at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only Serbia-side central bodies (Kancelarija za KiM, EPS) were confirmed as parallel-structure buyers publishing on Serbian national channels; no parallel municipal-level publication venue was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If parallel municipal spending is published nowhere, that spending is structurally invisible and must be inferred indirectly (media, Serbian budget line items, audit reports) rather than collected.

coverage_gaps.description: Only Severna Mitrovica's own municipal site was confirmed at URL level; the individual official sites of Zvecan, Zubin Potok, Leposavic, Gracanica, Strpce, Klokot, Ranilug, Partes and Novo Brdo were not individually resolved in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest the full municipality URL list from mapl.rks-gov.net/sr/portal-opstina/ and register each municipality's /sr/ procurement section as a separate source.

coverage_gaps.description: No Serbian-language audit source was covered: Kosovo's National Audit Office (ZKA/NKR) municipal audit reports and Serbia's DRI (Drzavna revizorska institucija) reports on Kancelarija za KiM both examine contracting and banking arrangements retrospectively.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add zka-rks.org (Serbian-language municipal audit reports) and dri.rs (reports covering KiM-funded bodies) as direct sources in a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: The supply side is uncovered: Serbian-language corporate registries and bank/vendor announcements (banks operating or formerly operating in Serb-majority areas - Komercijalna/NLB, Postanska stedionica, Jugobanka; Serbian payment integrators) were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ARBK/KBRA business registry (Serbian interface), APR (Serbia), and bank investor/press pages as indirect sources; use them to attribute award notices to real corporate entities.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival strategy was identified for Serbian-language Kosovo sources, which are unusually volatile (outlets close, municipal sites are restructured, notices are removed after award periods).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair every source in this cell with Wayback/archive.today snapshotting at collection time so award notices remain citable after removal.

coverage_gaps.description: Cyrillic-script querying was under-used: most searches ran in Serbian Latin, while Serbia-side institutional sources (NBS, kim.gov.rs, DRI) publish heavily in Cyrillic.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run the seed and glossary queries in Cyrillic (jавне набавке, обавештење о додели уговора, банкарске услуге, платни промет) and treat Latin/Cyrillic as two distinct retrieval channels.

brief: The Serbian-language channel around Kosovo procurement splits into two institutional spheres that must both be monitored: the Kosovo state sphere, which is legally obliged to publish tender and award notices in Serbian (e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net, OSHP review decisions, municipal /sr/ pages such as Severna Mitrovica, plus agency sites like PAK), and the Serbia-side parallel sphere, which publishes nowhere in the Kosovo system at all (Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju, EPS Elektrokosmet, NBS, all via jnportal.ujn.gov.rs and their own sites). Between them sits a dense, fast-moving Serbian-language media layer - KoSSev, Radio Kontakt Plus, Radio KIM, Gracanica Online, Kosovo Online, aggregated by kos-info.net and catalogued by Media Ownership Monitor - which is frequently the only public reporting on bank-branch closures, licensing status and dinar/euro payment restrictions in Serb-majority municipalities, and which is invisible to sq/en queries. General web search reliably finds these portals and the standard Serbian notice forms but not individual banking/payment award records, so production collection must run through portal-internal search and PDF harvesting rather than open-web crawling. The largest remaining gaps are per-municipality site coverage beyond North Mitrovica, Serbian-language audit reports (ZKA and Serbia's DRI), supplier-side registries, and Cyrillic-script retrieval.
